# harnessr

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/elkronos/readgpt/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/elkronos/readgpt/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![tests](https://github.com/elkronos/readgpt/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/elkronos/readgpt/actions/workflows/tests.yaml)

For one document,
[`answer_document()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_document.md)
picks an ingest, a segmentation and a reading strategy, and returns an
answer with a trace of everything it did. For a folder,
[`gr_screen()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_screen.md)
decides which documents count,
[`gr_extract()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_extract.md)
fills a typed schema across all of them, and
[`gr_synthesise()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_synthesise.md)
writes the result up with every claim citing the row it rests on. Every
model call is budgeted, recorded and checked, and can be cached.

harnessr was called readgpt up to version 0.6.0. The GitHub repository
keeps the old name. Requests, cache keys and recordings are unchanged by
the rename; the `readgpt.*` options are still read, with a warning (see
`NEWS.md`).

The [guides](#guides) explain each part in depth and all run offline,
without a key. Start with
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md).
They are also on the website, <https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/>,
with the reference for every function.

## Install

Requires R 4.1 or later. The only non-base hard dependencies are
`digest`, `httr` and `jsonlite`.

``` r

install.packages(c("remotes", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
remotes::install_github("elkronos/readgpt", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

`build_vignettes = TRUE` installs the guides, so
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md)
works. Building them needs `knitr`, `rmarkdown` and Pandoc. Pandoc comes
with RStudio; without RStudio, install it from
<https://pandoc.org/installing.html> first, or leave out
`build_vignettes = TRUE`. From a local checkout,
`remotes::install_local("path/to/readgpt")` does the same.

Other packages (pdftools, tesseract and magick, xml2, future, ellmer,
shiny) are checked when a feature needs them; a missing one is an error
naming it, unless harnessr can carry on without it.
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md)
lists them.

## Quick start

``` r

library(harnessr)

ans <- answer_document("report.pdf", "What was Q3 revenue?", recipe = "needle")
ans$answer
ans$partial
```

Every console block below is real output from the bundled example
document, with
[`gr_mock_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_mock_client.md)
standing in for the API, so you can reproduce all of it without a key.
[`gr_compare()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_compare.md)
runs several recipes over one document and extracts it only once, so you
can choose a pipeline before committing to it:

``` r

cl  <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
cmp <- gr_compare(gr_example(), "What was revenue in fiscal 2024?",
                  c("fast", "needle", "thorough", "survey"), client = cl)
cmp$summary[, c("recipe", "segmenter", "chunks", "reader", "signature", "settings")]
#>     recipe  segmenter chunks       reader         signature
#> 1     fast  paragraph      1        stuff        all|1|none
#> 2   needle   semantic      2     retrieve       topk|1|none
#> 3 thorough  paragraph      1   map_reduce   all|N+logN|tree
#> 4   survey structural      6 hierarchical all|N+tree+1|tree
#>                                                settings
#> 1                                       max_tokens=4000
#> 2 top_k=8, cite=TRUE, max_tokens=500, overlap_tokens=50
#> 3                                    overlap_tokens=120
#> 4                                       max_tokens=1500
```

`settings` names whatever each recipe changed from the defaults. The
bundled example is small (573 tokens as
[`gr_ingest()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ingest.md)
counts them), so `fast` and `thorough` fit it in one chunk. On a real
report they would not.

Or build a pipeline by hand, one choice per axis:

``` r

rec <- gr_recipe("my_pipeline",
  ingest  = list(clean = c("page_numbers", "hyphenation", "headers_footers")),
  segment = list(method = "structural", max_tokens = 800, overlap_tokens = 80),
  read    = list(reader = "skim", cite = TRUE, model = "gpt-5.6-terra"))

ans <- answer_document("thesis.pdf", "How was the sample recruited?", rec)
```

## Connecting a model

``` r

Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-...")   # or
options(harnessr.api_key = "sk-...")     # or
cl <- gr_client(api_key = "sk-...")     # per client, for multi-user Shiny
```

An explicit argument wins over the `harnessr.api_key` option, which wins
over `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Keep the key out of the repository: `.Renviron`
is the usual home for it, and both `.Renviron` and `.Rprofile` are
gitignored here. Without a key,
[`answer_document()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_document.md),
[`gr_read_many()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read_many.md)
and
[`gr_compare()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_compare.md)
stop before reading the document, with a `gr_auth_error` that says how
to set one, so a missing key does not first cost an OCR pass over a long
scan.

Behind a company gateway, `gr_client(headers = )` sends the headers it
wants, such as Azure’s `api-key`;
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md)
shows how.

The built-in client speaks to OpenAI-compatible `/responses` and
`/chat/completions` endpoints.
[`gr_ellmer_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ellmer_client.md)
hands the transport to [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/), which
covers roughly twenty providers, local models through Ollama among them.
The spending limit is on by default and can hold only for a model with a
registered price, so register the model the ellmer object was built
with, at your provider’s current prices in US dollars per million
tokens:

``` r

library(ellmer)

gr_register_model("claude-sonnet-4-5", context_window = 200000, max_output = 64000,
                  input_usd = 3, output_usd = 15)
cl <- gr_ellmer_client(chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-5"))
answer_document("report.pdf", "What was revenue?", "thorough", client = cl)

# A local model has no price to register, so let it run unpriced:
gr_options(allow_unpriced = TRUE)
gr_ellmer_client(chat_ollama(model = "llama3.1"))
```

Without a registered price, a run under `max_cost_usd` stops before its
first request with an `hr_unpriced_model` error.
[`vignette("runs")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.md)
covers unpriced models and what changes through ellmer (temperature and
embeddings).

Anything else, such as a model behind a queue, goes through
[`gr_backend_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_backend_client.md),
which makes any function of `messages` and `params` that returns a
string the transport. Limits, the trace, caching and replay work the
same way on every client. Register the model’s real context window with
[`gr_register_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_model.md),
since it is what sizes your chunks.

## How it works

How you break a document up and how you make the model read it are
separate decisions worth experimenting with, so the package keeps them
separate. There are three independent axes, each a registry you can
extend without editing the package:

      source  ──▶  INGEST  ──▶  SEGMENT  ──▶  READ  ──▶  answer + trace
                   │             │             │
                   │             │             └─ 12 strategies, each with a
                   │             │                distinct traversal signature
                   │             └─ 9 segmenters + overlap / min-size / context
                   └─ 6 extractors + 14 individually toggleable cleaners

Any ingest composes with any segmenter and any reader.
[`gr_recipe()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_recipe.md)
binds one of each into a named pipeline, and a recipe run alongside
others gives a byte-identical `$answer` and `$chunks_used` to running it
alone. Which model answers is a fourth, independent choice.

[`gr_ingest()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ingest.md)
turns a file into cleaned text blocks that keep their page and section.
The extractors cover plain text and delimited files, Markdown, HTML,
Word, PDF (with OCR for scanned pages) and images, and a web address is
downloaded and read as whatever it serves. Each cleaner can be turned on
or off by name, and `remove_numbers` is off by default, because it would
make every figure, date and percentage unanswerable. See
[`vignette("ingest")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/ingest.md).

[`gr_segment()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_segment.md)
cuts the document into chunks: on a ruler, by paragraph, sentence,
heading or page, where embeddings diverge, or by rewriting it into
standalone statements. `max_tokens` is enforced on every segmenter, and
[`gr_chunk_stats()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_chunk_stats.md)
compares chunkings for nothing before you spend anything on reading. See
[`vignette("segment")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/segment.md).

[`gr_read()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read.md)
answers the question with one of the strategies, from `stuff` (one
request carrying the whole document) through `map_reduce` (one per
chunk, then a merge) to `iterative` (multi-hop). Each has a traversal
signature, `select|calls|state`, which is how the package tells two
methods apart from two names for the same thing. Recipes such as `fast`,
`needle`, `thorough` and `survey` bundle a segmenter with a reader.
[`answer_document()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_document.md)
defaults to `"auto"`, which reads a document of up to 50,000 tokens
(less on a model with a small context window) with `fast` and a longer
one with `thorough`. See
[`vignette("readers")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/readers.md),
which also covers what to check when the answer is not what you
expected.

## What an answer gives back

`print(ans)` sums up the cost, where the evidence came from and, when
the answer is partial, why:

``` r

ans$answer
ans$partial                 # TRUE means something degraded; check this first
ans$notes                   # why: dropped_chunks, failed_calls, unread_pages, ...
ans$evidence                # the passages the answer rests on, with page and section
gr_verify_evidence(ans)     # whether each quoted passage is in its chunk
as.data.frame(ans$trace)    # one row per request: stage, tokens, usd, seconds, prompt, reply
```

A quotation that is not in the chunk it is attributed to marks the
answer partial, and a citation of a chunk that was never sent is
recorded in `ans$notes$cited_unknown`. Both checks are local string
operations, so they cost nothing and always run.

[`gr_trace_cost()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace_cost.md)
prices a run by each step’s own model and counts only the calls that
were issued;
[`vignette("runs")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.md)
shows a bill.

[`gr_audit_report()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_audit_report.md)
puts the question, the answer, whether it is partial and why, the cost,
and the passages in document order on one HTML page:

``` r

gr_audit_report("answer.html", answer = ans)
```

## Many documents and reviews

[`gr_read_many()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read_many.md)
runs one recipe over a folder and returns one row per document. An
unreadable file costs one row rather than the run, each document gets
its own budget, `max_total_calls` and `max_total_usd` bound the run, and
`store =` makes a long run resumable.

A review fixes its protocol before reading anything, then runs
[`gr_protocol()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_protocol.md)
→
[`gr_screen()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_screen.md)
→
[`gr_extract()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_extract.md)
→
[`gr_synthesise()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_synthesise.md).
Screening gives every document a decision and a reason, and sends
`"unclear"` ones to a person instead of guessing. Extraction gives a
typed table, and its `n_unverified` column counts the values in a row
that cannot be pointed at in the document. Where a document contradicts
itself, `conflicts` names the field and the earliest chunk’s value is
kept; `resolve = "model"` spends one call per disagreeing field to have
the model choose instead. The write-up cites `[study n]` for each row it
rests on, and every marker is checked against the rows that exist. The
audit report writes the whole chain out for the co-author or reviewer
who asks “how do you know?”:

``` r

gr_audit_report("audit.html", extraction = x, synthesis = review, claims = cm,
                protocol = protocol)
```

[`vignette("review")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/review.md)
covers the rest: surveying a folder with
[`gr_inventory()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_inventory.md),
starting from a reference manager’s export with
[`gr_records()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_records.md),
measuring the screener against a hand-screened sample with
[`gr_calibrate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_calibrate.md),
author-year citations, claims, outlines and gaps, and the checks on
revision passes.

## Limits and records

Two limits are on by default, `max_cost_usd = 5` and `max_calls = 400`
per run, set with
[`gr_options()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_options.md)
or held together by
[`hr_governor()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_governor.md).
Every request is checked before it is sent, against what the run has
spent plus the most that request could cost, and a request that could
pass a limit is not sent. The answer comes back partial, and the trace
names the limit in `stop_reason`.

[`gr_cache()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache.md)
stores each successful response, keyed on everything that can change the
reply, and
[`gr_cache_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache_client.md)
attaches it to a client, so a repeat is free and identical. A trace
records every prompt and response, so
[`gr_trace_save()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace_save.md)
and
[`gr_replay_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_replay_client.md)
reproduce a run from the saved trace and the source document, with no
key and no spend.

[`vignette("runs")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.md)
covers the other limits (tokens, output caps, allowed models), reasoning
effort per stage, what each trace step records, cache keys, replaying a
run that used embeddings, and the classed errors and warnings.

## Shiny app

``` r

shiny::runApp(system.file("shiny", package = "harnessr"))
```

Every axis is a control, and a free “Preview chunking” button shows the
chunks before you spend anything. Set `GPTREAD_DOC_ROOTS` before
exposing the app to anyone else: unset, it reads `~/Documents`, or your
whole home directory when there is none.
[`vignette("segment")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/segment.md)
has the details.

## Guides

Each guide is on the website and, once installed, in R as
`vignette("name")`.

| guide | what it covers |
|----|----|
| [Get started](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.html) (`harnessr`) | The ideas, installing, connecting, a first question checked from start to finish, cost, a glossary |
| [Getting text out of files](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/ingest.html) (`ingest`) | PDFs, Word files, web pages and scans, every cleaner, and surveying a folder |
| [Cutting documents into chunks](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/segment.html) (`segment`) | The segmenters, overlap, minimum size, context, and comparing chunkings |
| [Choosing how the model reads](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/readers.html) (`readers`) | The reading strategies, recipes, what each costs, and how to choose |
| [Many documents and literature reviews](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/review.html) (`review`) | Search, screening, calibration, extraction, claims, synthesis, the audit report |
| [Cost, limits and reproducible runs](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.html) (`runs`) | The governor, effort, traces, caching, replay |
| [Extending harnessr](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/extending.html) (`extending`) | Registering your own extractors, cleaners, segmenters, readers and embedders, and checking them |

## Development

``` bash
bash run-tests.sh   # install deps if needed, install, run the suite; --help lists the options
```

The suite needs `testthat` and `withr`, plus `future` and
`future.apply`, without which the tests of a parallel run’s call and
cost counts are skipped. Every test uses an offline mock client, so no
key is needed and no requests are made; `--check` runs a full
`R CMD check`.

| workflow | what it does |
|----|----|
| `tests.yaml` | installs, runs the suite, runs the README’s code blocks and diffs their documented output against real output, knits every guide with no key and no network, and checks the documented counts against the registries and that no two readers share a traversal signature |
| `R-CMD-check.yaml` | full `R CMD check` on macOS and Ubuntu, current R and the previous release |
| `pkgdown.yaml` | builds the website on pull requests and on pushes to the main branch, and publishes it except from a pull request |
| `pr-checks.yaml` | fails a pull request that drops an `expect_*()` call or adds a `skip()` without the label `tests-reviewed`, or adds a dependency without the label `deps-reviewed` (an added package must be on CRAN either way), and lints the changed files under `R/` |

`Rscript dev/ci/pr-checks.R tests origin/main HEAD` runs the
pull-request checks locally. No workflow needs a secret:
`OPENAI_API_KEY` is empty, or a dummy value for the README blocks, so a
real key can never change a result.

## Migrating from v1

The old entry points still work and map onto the new pipeline, warning
once:

| v1 | now |
|----|----|
| `answer_question(f, q, mode = "Chunked")` | `answer_document(f, q, "thorough")` |
| `parse_text(f, chunk_method = "semantic")` | `gr_ingest(f)` → `gr_segment(doc, "semantic")` |
| [`gpt_read_chunked()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_chunked.md) | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "map_reduce")` |
| [`gpt_read_retrieval()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_retrieval.md) | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "skim")` |
| [`gpt_read_hierarchical()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_hierarchical.md) | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "hierarchical")` |
| [`gpt_read_multipass()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_multipass.md) | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "ensemble")` |

Three behaviour changes are deliberate and will alter your results:

1.  **`mode` no longer defaults to all five modes.**
    `answer_question(f, q)` in v1 ran every mode: 41 API calls on an
    8-paragraph document, where one was expected.
2.  **Modes no longer contaminate each other.** In v1,
    `mode = c("Chunked", "Semantic")` changed Chunked’s chunking, its
    cost, and its answer relative to `mode = "Chunked"` alone.
3.  **Digits are no longer stripped by default.** v1’s
    `remove_numbers = TRUE` default was unreachable from
    [`answer_question()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_question.md),
    so every figure, date and percentage was deleted before the model
    saw the document.

v1’s `refine = TRUE` is mapped to citations only. Its verification pass
is not reproduced because it could never run: it called a
`search_text()` function that was never defined anywhere in the
repository.

The v1 source is kept under `legacy/` for reference and A/B comparison.
It is not loaded by the package. To reproduce its ingestion and chunking
under the current code, use the `legacy` recipe, which reproduces its
digit stripping, 3000-token paragraph chunks and lack of overlap. The
regression suite in `tests/testthat/` reproduces each of these defects
against the current code.

# Package index

## Ask a question

Start here. One call reads a document and answers a question, and the
answer says what it rests on and whether anything went wrong. See
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md).

- [`answer_document()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_document.md)
  : Answer a question about a document
- [`gr_answer`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_answer.md)
  : The result of one reading run
- [`is_not_found()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/is_not_found.md)
  : Did the model report that the document does not contain the answer?
- [`gr_example()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_example.md)
  : Path to the bundled example document
- [`gr_recipes()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_recipes.md)
  : Ready-made recipes
- [`gr_recipe()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_recipe.md)
  : Bind an ingestion, segmentation and reading configuration together
- [`gr_compare()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_compare.md)
  : Run several recipes over one document and compare them

## Connect to a model

Clients for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, any provider ellmer supports,
any function you write, and an offline stand-in for practice and tests.
See
[`vignette("harnessr")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/harnessr.md)
and the README.

- [`gr_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_client.md)
  : Construct a model client
- [`gr_api_key()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_api_key.md)
  : Resolve the API key
- [`gr_ellmer_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ellmer_client.md)
  : Read documents through an ellmer chat
- [`gr_backend_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_backend_client.md)
  : Use any function as the model transport
- [`gr_mock_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_mock_client.md)
  : A deterministic offline client for tests, demos and dry runs
- [`gr_call()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_call.md)
  : Call a model
- [`gr_result`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_result.md)
  : The result of one model call
- [`gr_models()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_models.md)
  : List every known model
- [`gr_model_info()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_model_info.md)
  : Look up a model's capabilities
- [`gr_model_limits()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_model_limits.md)
  : Context and output limits for a model
- [`gr_register_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_model.md)
  : Register a model (or override a built-in entry)

## Get text out of files

Extraction, cleaning and a survey of a folder before anything is spent.
See
[`vignette("ingest")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/ingest.md).

- [`gr_ingest()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ingest.md)
  : Ingest a document into cleaned, provenance-bearing text blocks
- [`gr_ingest_spec()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ingest_spec.md)
  : Describe an ingestion configuration
- [`gr_document`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_document.md)
  : An ingested document
- [`gr_extractors()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_extractors.md)
  : List registered extractors
- [`gr_cleaners()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cleaners.md)
  : List registered cleaners
- [`gr_clean()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_clean.md)
  : Run the cleaning pipeline over a character vector
- [`gr_inventory()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_inventory.md)
  : What is in a folder, before you read any of it

## Cut documents into chunks

The segmenters, their settings, and the free statistics for comparing
chunkings. See
[`vignette("segment")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/segment.md).

- [`gr_segment()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_segment.md)
  : Segment a document into chunks
- [`gr_segment_spec()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_segment_spec.md)
  : Describe a segmentation configuration
- [`gr_segmenters()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_segmenters.md)
  : List registered segmentation strategies
- [`gr_chunks`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_chunks.md)
  : A set of document chunks
- [`gr_chunk_stats()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_chunk_stats.md)
  : Summary statistics for a chunk set

## Read the chunks

The reading strategies, the settings that choose and place chunks, and
the check on quoted evidence. See
[`vignette("readers")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/readers.md).

- [`gr_read()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read.md)
  : Read chunks and answer a question
- [`gr_read_spec()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read_spec.md)
  : Describe a reading configuration
- [`gr_readers()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_readers.md)
  : List registered reading strategies
- [`gr_reader_signature()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_reader_signature.md)
  : The traversal signature of a reader
- [`gr_embed()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_embed.md)
  : Embed texts
- [`gr_embedders()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_embedders.md)
  : List registered embedding backends
- [`gr_verify_evidence()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_verify_evidence.md)
  : Check that quoted evidence really is in the document

## Many documents and literature reviews

One question over many documents, and a review from a search export to
screened studies, an extraction table, a written review and an audit
report, with the screening measured against a hand-screened sample. See
[`vignette("review")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/review.md).

- [`gr_read_many()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_read_many.md)
  : Ask one question of many documents
- [`gr_protocol()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_protocol.md)
  : Write down what a review is looking for
- [`gr_protocols()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_protocols.md)
  : Protocols that ship with the package, and any you have registered
- [`gr_protocol_save()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_protocol_save.md)
  [`gr_protocol_read()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_protocol_save.md)
  : Save a protocol to a file, and read one back
- [`gr_register_protocol()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_protocol.md)
  : Register a protocol
- [`gr_search()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_search.md)
  : Record how the search was run
- [`gr_records()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_records.md)
  : Read a search export, and say what the search found
- [`gr_screen()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_screen.md)
  : Decide which documents a review should read
- [`gr_reference()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_reference.md)
  : Draw a sample to screen by hand
- [`gr_calibrate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_calibrate.md)
  : Measure the screener against a hand-screened sample
- [`gr_resolve()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_resolve.md)
  : Record a person's decision on screened records
- [`` `[`( ``*`<gr_reference_frame>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/sub-.gr_reference_frame.md)
  : Subsetting a reference frame gives a plain data frame.
- [`gr_fields()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_fields.md)
  : Build an extraction schema
- [`gr_field()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_field.md)
  : Describe one field of an extraction schema
- [`gr_extract()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_extract.md)
  : Extract a typed schema from many documents
- [`gr_claims()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_claims.md)
  : The claims a table of studies supports
- [`gr_outline()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_outline.md)
  : Derive a review's sections from its claims
- [`gr_outline_pick()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_outline_pick.md)
  : Choose one of the outlines gr_outline() compared
- [`gr_gaps()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_gaps.md)
  : What a body of work does not cover
- [`gr_synthesise()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_synthesise.md)
  : Write a review from an extraction table
- [`gr_flow()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_flow.md)
  : Count what happened to every document
- [`gr_audit_report()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_audit_report.md)
  : Write the run out as an auditable report

## Cost, limits and tracing

Settings and spending limits, token counts and cost estimates, and the
trace every run records. See
[`vignette("runs")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.md).

- [`gr_options()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_options.md)
  : Get or set package options

- [`hr_governor()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_governor.md)
  : Limits on what a run may send

- [`gr_estimate_cost()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_estimate_cost.md)
  : Estimate the USD cost of a set of calls

- [`gr_count_tokens()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_count_tokens.md)
  : Count tokens in text

- [`gr_tokenizer()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_tokenizer.md)
  : The active tokenizer

- [`gr_set_tokenizer()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_set_tokenizer.md)
  : Register or inspect the active tokenizer

- [`gr_truncate_tokens()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_truncate_tokens.md)
  :

  Truncate text to at most `n` tokens

- [`gr_budget()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_budget.md)
  : Compute a usable input-token budget for one model call

- [`gr_trace()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<gr_trace>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace.md)
  : Create a run trace

- [`gr_trace_summary()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace_summary.md)
  : Summarise a trace

- [`gr_trace_cost()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace_cost.md)
  : What a run actually cost

- [`gr_trace_save()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_trace_save.md)
  : Save a trace to a file

- [`as_json()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/as_json.md)
  : Serialise an object to JSON

## Caching and replaying runs

Paying for a request once, and replaying a recorded run without a model.
See
[`vignette("runs")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/runs.md).

- [`gr_cache()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache.md)
  : A response cache
- [`gr_cache_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache_client.md)
  : Attach a cache to a client
- [`gr_cache_stats()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache_stats.md)
  : Cache statistics
- [`gr_cache_clear()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_cache_clear.md)
  : Delete every entry in a cache
- [`gr_flush_caches()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_flush_caches.md)
  : Clear the session's document and embedding caches
- [`gr_replay_client()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_replay_client.md)
  : A client that answers from a recorded run

## Extending harnessr

Every axis is a registry, and an addition is used exactly like a
built-in. See
[`vignette("extending")`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/articles/extending.md).

- [`gr_register_extractor()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_extractor.md)
  : Register a document extractor

- [`gr_register_cleaner()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_cleaner.md)
  : Register a cleaning step

- [`gr_register_segmenter()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_segmenter.md)
  : Register a segmentation strategy

- [`gr_register_reader()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_reader.md)
  : Register a reading strategy

- [`gr_register_embedder()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_register_embedder.md)
  : Register an embedding backend

- [`new_chunks()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/new_chunks.md)
  :

  Build a `gr_chunks`, the object every segmenter must return

- [`new_answer()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/new_answer.md)
  :

  Build a `gr_answer`, the object every reader must return

- [`hr_cost()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_cost.md)
  : What one run of a module can cost

- [`hr_schema()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_schema.md)
  : Collect parameters into a schema

- [`hr_param()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_param.md)
  : Declare one parameter of a module or spec

- [`hr_validate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_validate.md)
  : Validate and resolve settings against a schema

- [`hr_check_module()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/hr_check_module.md)
  : Check a module against a set of rules

- [`gr_check_reader()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_check_reader.md)
  : Check a reader against the reader contract

- [`gr_check_segmenter()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_check_segmenter.md)
  : Check a segmenter against the segmenter contract

## Superseded

The entry points of the first version, and the old name of
[`gr_example()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_example.md).
They still work and warn once; new code should use
[`answer_document()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_document.md),
[`gr_ingest()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_ingest.md),
[`gr_segment()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_segment.md)
and
[`gr_example()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gr_example.md).
The README’s “Migrating from v1” section maps each one.

- [`answer_question()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/answer_question.md)
  : Deprecated: answer a question using v1 mode names
- [`parse_text()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/parse_text.md)
  : Deprecated: parse a document into text chunks
- [`gpt_read_chunked()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_chunked.md)
  : Deprecated: chunk-by-chunk reading
- [`gpt_read_hierarchical()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_hierarchical.md)
  : Deprecated: hierarchical reading
- [`gpt_read_multipass()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_multipass.md)
  : Deprecated: multi-pass reading
- [`gpt_read_retrieval()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/gpt_read_retrieval.md)
  : Deprecated: evidence-extraction reading
- [`readgpt_example()`](https://elkronos.github.io/readgpt/reference/readgpt_example.md)
  : Deprecated: path to the bundled example document
